note: A sibling of ordering-vectors.json, not a part of it, because that file pins one property of the last-matching-pattern order (a last-segment bucket is a candidate source, never an answer) and every one of its cases is decided by the last matching line of one file. These cases pin the scope of a directory-only rule and the walk: a directory-only pattern is a fact about a directory, so it never matches a file below that directory by name (an excluded ancestor is what excludes a file, and a negation inside an excluded directory cannot re-open anything). git is the raw verdict and gitRule the line git named; expect is the three-valued answer all three implementations give. Paths exist on disk when the oracle runs, because only a real tree makes git answer a directory-ness question the way a caller would.
